content.content:
# Stacking verdict fusion — Raman × transport

*Investigation — consumes the locked output contracts of two sibling
investigations on the same device: a transport stacking call
(`trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`, `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md`, or
`trilayer-stacking-id.md`, per-channel — the device card's material line
routes) and a Raman call (`raman-stacking-id.md`, per-spot, stage-stamped) — and
produces a fused per-region verdict. Small by design: the modality
knowledge lives in the two base recipes; this recipe owns only the
reconciliation logic.*

## What

A region-resolved fused stacking verdict for one device, with every
agreement and disagreement classified by mechanism. **Verdicts are never
averaged; evidence is fused.** A traceable disagreement is a first-class
result, not a failure of either modality.

## When

Both modalities' contracts exist for one device. Fusion is evidential only
if each call was produced **without sight of the other** — verify this
first; if either call could have been shaped by the other, the fusion
degrades to a consistency narrative and says so.

## Why

The modalities are complementary, and differ on exactly the axes that
matter on mixed-domain flakes:

- **Transport**: in-situ on the **finished** device; probes the channel
  between a contact pair — a weighted average over whatever domains span
  it; blind to where domains sit.
- **Raman**: spot-resolved µm-scale geometry, but taken at **build stage
  S** (typically pre-fab), blind below the spot size, and perishable —
  post-map processing moves domain walls (base recipe, stage-stamping).

So fusion is **spatial and temporal reconciliation**, and the key
asymmetry is directional: documented conversion runs
**rhombohedral→Bernal only** (strain/chemistry/heat destabilize the
metastable rhombohedral order; the reverse is undocumented — converter
list in `raman-stacking-id.md`). A Raman-rhombohedral region can
legitimately measure Bernal later; a Raman-Bernal region that measures
rhombohedral cannot be explained by conversion.

## Recipe

**Step 1 — admissibility.** Both contracts carry weight words, evidence
lists, and coordinates (transport: which contact pair/channel; Raman:
spot/region positions + stage stamp, preferably with the region
mask/raster artifact — prose ranges force a re-derivation that
reproduces geography but not boundary pixels). A bare verdict without
evidence coordinates is not fusible — return it to its recipe.

**Step 2 — spatial registration (binding: produce the artifact).** Place
the Raman spots/regions and the transport channels on one device image or
coordinate frame. Use every supplied frame bridge: stage-registered
video images inside the Raman files, marker-frame optical images, and
the device GDS (exact pad/contact geometry beats a lead census read off
imagery — but identify gate leads vs channel leads from layer overlaps
before trusting the census). Across a transfer/pickup boundary do not
assume one rigid transform: fit multiple independent anchors; if they
disagree beyond their fit error (non-rigid strain), carry the
anchor-variant spread as the registration uncertainty and run the
stress audit over the variants. For each transport channel, classify
its Raman coverage: **covered / partial / uncovered**, with
registration uncertainty stated against the domain scale (a
µm-registration error on µm domains can flip a region's label — if
uncertainty ≳ domain scale, coverage is at best partial; it can also
leave a covered footprint's domain *composition* unresolved, which
limits the row the same way). Uncovered stays uncovered — no
interpolation from neighboring spots.

**Step 3 — temporal registration.** From the Raman stage stamp: list the
build steps between map and measurement, tagged by conversion risk
(metal deposition on/near the region > transfer/pickup > chemical+bake >
clean thermal). When maps exist at multiple build stages, difference
them: a region's evolution between two maps is direct evidence and
replaces risk-class inference for the steps they bracket
(directionality still binds — see Why). **Difference only
like-conditioned maps** (same through-stack status): a through-stack
superposition shifts the apparent metrics — apparatus, not evolution —
and differencing unlike stages manufactures wall motion. Assess each
stage's through-stack status separately; the gate-clean stage carries
the buried-channel call.

**Step 4 — per-region fusion.** For each named transport channel, one
row: transport verdict+strength | Raman verdict+strength+stage | fused
verdict+strength | mechanism class. A footprint straddling multiple
Raman verdicts splits into share sub-rows (each share ± its
registration spread), classified separately — the channel's fused
verdict follows the share picture, never an average. Classes:

- **Concordant** — verdicts agree: fused strength = the stronger, noting
  the agreement is across independent physics (band structure read
  electrically and optically) — the strongest evidence class this recipe
  produces.
- **Reconciled-by-conversion** — Raman rhombohedral, transport Bernal,
  and Step 3 names a risky intervening step: both calls stand (Raman
  true at stage S, transport true now); the channel's fused verdict
  *and strength* follow transport; the region is recorded as "converted
  (consistent-with), step ⟨X⟩". Without a named risky step this class is
  unavailable — don't invoke conversion as a free pass.
- **Reconciled-by-geometry** — verdicts differ and registration shows
  the modalities probed different regions (partial/uncovered channel, or
  sub-spot mixing flagged in the Raman contract): no conflict; report
  per-region, resist the urge to produce a per-device headline.
- **Single-modality** — one leg is uninformative or uncovered for the
  channel (a Hall pair with no stacking read, an unmapped channel):
  report the informative leg with its stage stamp, no fused upgrade. A
  Bernal-family Raman verdict propagates to measurement time
  (conversion directionality); a rhombohedral one does not — it stays
  "as of stage S".
- **Unreconciled** — Raman Bernal vs transport rhombohedral (conversion
  cannot explain), or same-region strong-vs-strong conflict with no mechanism:
  a **fork to report** (STYLE rule 14) with the deciding follow-up
  (near-field imaging of the region; re-map through the encapsulant;
  the transport cross-checks in the base recipe). One modality being
  wrong is now the *hypothesis set*, not an embarrassment — list which
  specific misread each contract's hedges already allow.

**Step 5 — the call.** Output contract: the Step 4 table (every named
channel), per-region fused verdicts on the strength scale, the
registration artifact, named hedges (registration uncertainty, uncovered
channels, stage gap), and what-would-settle for every unreconciled row.
**A fused "cannot tell" or a well-evidenced disagreement is a successful
outcome; forcing concordance is a protocol violation.**

## Verify

- **Independence audit** (Step 1's precondition): confirm from the
  contracts' provenance that neither call cites the other's evidence.
- **Registration stress**: shift the registration by its stated
  uncertainty (over the anchor variants, when the uncertainty is a
  spread); any region whose conclusion flips — mechanism class,
  coverage label, or domain share — is reported as
  registration-limited, not classified. The stable part of a split row
  (e.g. a majority share) may still be classified.
- **Directionality audit**: every reconciled-by-conversion row names its
  risky step; every Raman-Bernal/transport-rhombohedral row is in unreconciled (no
  exceptions — this asymmetry is the recipe's one hard rule).
- **No-averaging audit**: no fused strength exceeds its strongest input
  except the concordant class; no per-device verdict exists unless all
  covered regions concur.

## Examples

*(our-measurement — mechanical lessons only.)*

- QC0426 case
  (`hera/docs/notes/2026-07-17-QC0426-raman-fusion/fusion/` + the
  correction in the archive README): initially fused as concordant-ABA;
  PI review then identified the Raman leg as gate-contaminated (post-fab
  map through graphite gates), and the rows were re-labeled
  **transport-dominant** with Raman as weak corroboration. Two lessons:
  (1) **fusion inherits its inputs' physics misses** — the admissibility
  step checks contract *form*, not physics; the base recipes' screens
  (here, the through-stack screen) are the only defense, and a
  concordance is only as strong as its weaker leg's validity domain.
  (2) Imagery-based stage inference is consistent-with at best — this
  run's "no visible gate overlay ⇒ pre-top-gate" revision was overturned
  by grower testimony (graphite gates are near-invisible optically);
  report a stage conflict as a fork, not a revision. What stands: the
  registration work (lead census, ±1.5 µm measured) and both returned
  findings.
- QC0426 pre-fab ladder
  (`hera/docs/notes/2026-07-25-QC0426-prefab-raman/`): three-stage map
  series (flake → stack → device) on one device — the Step 3
  multi-stage case. The registration chain to contact pairs runs flake
  video frame → stack imagery → marked-chip optical images → GDS; the
  flake↔stack link across pickup (flake tears into ribbons) is the
  registration-uncertainty driver.
- Synthetic four-class mechanics fixture
  (`hera/models/raman_stacking/dryrun/fusion/`): re-runnable regression
  covering all four mechanism classes and the audits — run it after any
  edit to this recipe.

## Next

- Unreconciled rows → price the deciding measurement before more
  argument; near-field imaging resolves what both far-field modalities
  cannot.
- Concordant mixed-domain maps → the fused domain picture (which pairs
  probe which stacking) feeds campaign planning in the transport
  recipe's Next section.

# Raman / fab record — VTI-02

*Pre-fab prior, not ground truth. Raman was taken on the parent flake
before stacking; no Raman at any later stage (no exposed device layer
after gating). Stacking, anneal, cut, and litho all postdate the read,
each an ABC→ABA conversion risk.*

## Provenance

- Fabricated by: Ben
- Parent flake: https://flakes.sharpelab.science/scanInspector/244?flake=84135
- Raman acquisition date: unknown
- Build stage at acquisition: pre-stacking, on parent flake
- Instrument / conditions: <spectrometer, wavelength, spot size — unknown, ask Ben>

## Raman findings

The Raman indicates a domain of rhombohedral that was subsequently
isolated. The rhombohedral domain survived the cutting process but no
further Raman was performed during device assembly.

Some spectra look like noise due to the laser cutting.

- Flakemap / spectra files: not yet in hand — pending from Ben

## Cut and device region

We cut out the rhombohedral domain and expect the cut region to contain
no ABA.

## Overall pre-fab lean

- Lean: ABC (isolated rhombohedral domain prior to stacking)
- Strength: strong
=========== DEVICE CARD ===========
# Device card — vti-02 (tetralayer graphene)

*Session device card for vti-02 on the **VTI** cryostat. Deployed into the
measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
**physical truth**: what is wired, the hardware, the outer safety box,
the provided gate operating limits, and the provided contact
configuration. The CNP location and (n, D) calibration are established
in-session (see the session brief).*

## Identity
- **Device id**: `vti-02`
- **Material**: tetralayer graphene (`4LGr`).
- **Owner**: Aaron
- **Fridge**: VTI (variable-temperature insert). Base (sample)
  temperature ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.
- **Status**: cold, wired — hardwired breakout, no contact mux; no CNP
  location on record.

## Gate stack
- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by a Keithley 2400**
  (`k_2400_tg`) — sweeps use `k_tg.volt` (5 mV step pacing; the measure
  notebook's setup cells bind `k_tg`).
- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): graphite on hBN, driven by the second
  **Keithley 2400** (`k_2400_bg`).
- **Si global back gate** (`k_si`): doped-Si gate through **SiO₂**,
  driven by the **SRS DC205** — bound directly to the driver's ramped
  parameter **`dc205.smart_voltage`** (set ramps at `ramp_rate = 0.5`
  V/s, get reads back `VOLT?`; data column **`dc205_smart_voltage`**).
  The DC205 has **no current readback** — gate-leakage monitoring lives
  on the Keithley `curr` channels (TG/BG) only. `ramp_voltage` steps
  span/50: a full ±50 V traverse moves in ~1 V steps, paced by
  `ramp_rate`. The graphite back gate screens Si from the channel — Si
  couples only to the contacts (contact-doping gate). Operating limit
  provided (below).
- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
  ```python
  from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages
  c_tg = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)])           # 9.5 nm hBN
  c_bg = stack_capacitance([(11, 3), (0, 3.9)])   # 11 nm hBN, no SiO2 term
  ```
  Treat anything derived from these (lever arms, n/D scales, CNP-line
  slope) as uncalibrated until the session's own gate map confirms it.

## Gate operating limits — gate B contract

Gate operating limits for the session:

| Parameter | Operating limit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `k_tg.volt` | **[−0.3, +1.0] V** | provided; geometry ceiling is the hard fence behind it |
| `k_bg.volt` | **[−1.3, +2.0] V** | provided |
| `dc205.smart_voltage` / `dc205.voltage` (Si) | **[−25, +25] V** | provided; DC205 must be on its ±100 V range (RNGE 2) |
| **B field (session cap)** | **\|B\| ≤ 10.0 T** | committed on the `magnet.field` validator (SAFETIES); driver `max_field_T = 14.0` T is the hard backstop |
| **T setpoint (session cap)** | **`set_both` target ≤ 100 K** | provided; committed as a SAFETIES setpoint typo-guard cap. `ratio = 0.95` per the rig card — deviations consent-gated |

## Measurement setup (rig instruments wired this cooldown)
- **Gates**: top via **k_2400_tg** (GPIB0::1), back via **k_2400_bg**
  (GPIB0::24), hardwired to their sources.
- **Si gate**: **DC205** (`dc205.smart_voltage`, ASRL7, ±100 V
  range), hardwired to its source.
- **AC excitation / lock-ins**: SR830 family (`sr0` GPIB0::22, `sr1` GPIB0::14, `sr2` GPIB0::19, `sr3` GPIB0::18).
  Current-bias drive through a **100 MOhm** bias resistor, lock-in
  frequency **13.777 Hz**.
- **Current channel**: **`sr0`** = drain current, **`sr0_gain = −1E6`**
  (preamp gain). Per-channel sensitivities are recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **Drive / bias channel**: **`sr1`** — the lock-in whose
  oscillator provides the current-bias drive; `I_bias` = its live amplitude
  / the bias resistor. `hera-watch` reads the drive here.
- **Contacts — hardwired, no mux this cooldown**: device pads bond to
  two Fischer cables and land on the breakout; instrument leads connect
  directly there. Contact roles are **fixed** — rerouting a pair is
  operator work at the breakout, not software.
  - **Contact map**:

    Bonded pads (label = position, T = top arc L→R, B = left side then
    bottom L→R). Only the provided configuration below is wired to
    instruments this cooldown:

    | Label | Pad | | Label | Pad |

# THE CALL (revised after run 8) — vti-02 stacking

Supersedes the run-7 verdict above, which read **ABAB (consistent-with)**. Run 8
converts that to a call. Output contract per
`investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 7, all five parts.

## 1. Per-region verdict

> **channel B_1−B_2: ABAB (strong).**
>
> Tetralayer Bernal stacking, with symmetry-allowed inter-block magnetic
> breakdown producing the tone at F_L.

The investigation's stated criterion for *strong* is "two branches on the ABAB
curves **and** the F_L-tone origin passed". Both are met below.

One region only — T_1…T_4 are dead, so there is a single live four-terminal pair
and **no mosaic test is possible on this cooldown**. "Per-region" means "the one
region we can see".

## 2. Evidence

Electron side, D ≈ 0, T ≈ 1.20 K, B = 1 → 8 T uniform in 1/B, δF = 1.143 T,
57 density columns, τ = 300 ms.

**(a) A pair partitioning F_L, reproducible in every extraction.** Recurrence
over 18 extraction choices (6 field windows × 3 background degrees):

| n (10¹² cm⁻²) | F_L (T) | light | heavy | sum tone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.29 | 23.7 | 4.9 T (18/18, 0.21) | 17.7 T (18/18, 0.75) | 22.3 T (18/18, 0.94) |
| 2.69 | 27.8 | 5.9 T (18/18, 0.21) | 20.4 T (18/18, 0.74) | 26.3 T (18/18, 0.95) |
| 3.05 | 31.5 | 7.6 T (18/18, 0.24) | 22.5 T (18/18, 0.71) | 29.9 T (18/18, 0.95) |

**18/18 reproducibility**, against 3–9/18 for the same partner tones in run 7.
The Luttinger sum closes (< 8%) in **39 of 57 columns**.

**(b) The F_L tone is a breakdown orbit, not an ABCA singleton.** This is the
discrimination the investigation makes *mandatory* before any singleton call, and
which run 7 could not perform. Splitting the record at its 1/B midpoint (B =
1.778 T) gives two halves of equal δF = 2.29 T, and comparing the sum tone's
amplitude against the heavy fundamental in each half:

| n (10¹²) | low-B half | high-B half | ratio | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.55 | 0.27 | 7.79 | 29.4 | breakdown |
| 2.72 | 0.74 | 8.36 | 11.3 | breakdown |
| 2.88 | 0.33 | 2.60 | 7.8 | breakdown |
| 3.05 | 0.54 | 3.59 | 6.7 | breakdown |

**13 testable columns: 10 breakdown-like, 0 pocket-like, 3 flat; median ratio
6.66.** The tone at F_L strengthens 5–30× with field relative to the
fundamentals, while a genuine pocket would keep its own Dingle envelope. **Zero
columns behave like a real pocket.** ABAB inter-block breakdown is
symmetry-allowed at N = 4 (no parity protection between the two bilayer-like
blocks), so this is the expected configuration, not an exotic one.

**(c) The partition tracks the ABAB curves across density, and excludes
adjacent-N.** The mandatory dual overlay:

| n (10¹²) | measured frac | ABAB-4L | trilayer ML+BL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.60 | 0.169 | 0.141 | 0.015 |
| 2.26 | 0.210 | 0.186 | 0.034 |
| 2.92 | 0.240 | 0.213 | 0.051 |
| 3.05 | 0.252 | 0.216 | 0.054 |

Mean |measured − model|: **ABAB-4L 0.025 vs trilayer 0.175 — tracks ABAB by
6.9×**. The partner fraction *rises* with density along the ABAB curve; this is
the trajectory test the investigation demands, not a single-point ratio match
(it warns the fractions cross near |n| ≈ 2×10¹², so magnitude alone cannot
decide). Transport supports **N = 4 over N = 3** decisively.

**(d) The whole peak set closes under one global scale.** The sum tone sits at
0.95·F_L rather than 1.00. A **single global density rescale of 1.05** — inside
my own lever-arm error (1.4% on c_tg, 6% on c_bg) and far inside the recipe's
0.8–1.2 band — puts the set at **0.22 / 0.78 with the sum at 1.00**, against the
ABAB model's **0.216 / 0.784**. The scale was fitted to the whole set, not to one
tone.

**(e) g = 4 verified in-data.** The calibration fans' LL ray slopes fall in ratio
4:8:12:16:20:24 with slope/ν consistent to 1.4% (run 5), so the four-fold
degeneracy underlying F_L = (h/4e)·n is measured. Degeneracy audit passes.

## 3. Confidence and hedges

**Confidence: high for ABAB on this region and this carrier sign.** The three
independent legs — reproducible pair, breakdown-discriminated F_L tone,
ABAB-tracking trajectory — agree, and each individually excludes a different
alternative (noise, ABCA, adjacent-N).

Hedges, each of which remains genuinely open:

- **The decisive per-branch mass test was not done.** ABAB's branches differ by
  ≈ φ² ≈ 2.6× in cyclotron mass, and the investigation calls the LK mass split
  *decisive* for separating two genuine bands from one band plus an artifact.
  Everything here is frequency-domain. This is the single biggest gap.
- **Single field polarity, ~1% R_xy admixture** (R_xx runs negative at deep
  minima, scaling as h/νe²). No ±B symmetrisation was possible. R_xy is periodic
  in 1/B at the *same* fundamental, so it distorts harmonic content but does not
  create new fundamentals — the pair positions and the partition are robust to
  it; the harmonic tones (≈ 1.8–1.9·F_L, and 15.0 T ≈ 2 × 7.6 T at n = 3.05) are
  not, and no claim rests on them.
- **Electron side only.** The hole side is gate-window-limited to −0.97×10¹²,
  inside the exception regime where the ABAB pair is close and balanced. Not
  measured in this fan at all. **Reported as unmeasured, not as a null.**
- **Absolute density scale rests on assigning Δν = 4 to the lowest LL ray.** The
  ray ratios fix the spacing, not the absolute; the cross-check is the implied
  top-gate hBN of 10.56 nm against the card's 9.50 (Δν = 6 → 7.0 nm, Δν = 3 →
  14.1 nm, both far worse). A consistency argument, not a measurement — and it is
  load-bearing, since the 1.05 rescale in (d) is only defensible because the
  lever arm came from exact LL degeneracy.
- **18 of 57 columns do not close the Luttinger sum**, and only 13 columns were
  testable for the breakdown discrimination (a resolvable sum tone plus a closing
  pair in *both* halves is a demanding requirement). The call rests on the
  columns that pass, and the failures are concentrated at low |n| where the light
  tone approaches δF.
- **One region, no mosaic test.** A single live pair cannot detect stacking
  domains elsewhere on the flake.

## 4. What would firm it further

1. **Per-branch LK masses** (`temperature-dependence-vti`, Flavor B) — the
   decisive test, and the obvious next session. Expect ≈ 2.6× between branches.
2. **±B symmetrisation** to remove the R_xy admixture and clean the harmonic
   structure.
3. **Hole side**, which needs a wider *negative* top-gate range — worth checking
   whether −0.3 V was a conservative provided limit or a physical one.
4. **A second Rxx pair** (operator rewiring at the breakout) to make a
   mosaic/per-region statement possible at all.

## 5. Status

**This is a call, not a lean.** vti-02, in the region probed by B_1−B_2, on the
electron side at D ≈ 0, is **Bernal (ABAB) tetralayer graphene** exhibiting
symmetry-allowed inter-block magnetic breakdown. Per the investigation's `Next`:
ABAB-confirmed means conventional tetralayer — the flat-band / correlated /
superconducting physics that motivates ABCA hunting is **not** here, and campaign
value lies in QH degeneracy-lifting or even-N interaction physics if the device is
clean enough, otherwise deprioritise.

# Trilayer stacking identification from Raman data (ABA vs ABC)

*Investigation — reads **supplied** Raman spectra or hyperspectral maps of a
trilayer-graphene flake/device and produces a spot-resolved stacking call.
This modality is data-analysis, not instrument-driving: the acquisition
already happened, usually on another instrument at another time — which is
why acquisition metadata and build-stage provenance are load-bearing inputs,
not details.*

**References**: the three ingested papers ground every claim —
`hera/docs/papers/1011.3021/paper.md` (Lui 2011 — 2D lineshape + FWHM

  is strong; *magnitude* of the split (≳ 10 cm⁻¹ between population

  magnitude heuristic — the pattern sets the grade and the split size

  excitation. At in-zone excitation treat the M read as uninformative —
  direction-inverted signatures are expected there, not anomalies.

  channels at ~zero (PI review, 2026-07-17) — they stay here as

  FWHM(G) maps 18–24 cm⁻¹ window). **Confounds**: strain and doping both

  acquired).** ABA: C mode ~33 cm⁻¹, ABC: C′ ~19 cm⁻¹ — symmetry-

  coverage, this alone can settle a spot.

  count (optical contrast / prior characterization) before reading width
  as stacking. A thickness terrace inside the map is the first
  alternative hypothesis for any "domain wall".

  but µm-scale domains are common (Lui: ~40% of trilayers mixed, none
  purely ABC), so walls crossing the ~µm spot are the norm: a spot
  straddling a wall gives a linear combination (Lui SI), which FWHM

walls move by µm** (citation, Geisenhof AANM 2 6067), hBN pickup along

subsequent build steps; a pre-fab map constrains the finished device only
modulo those steps.

within-one-map two-population split carrying the classification (Bernal
widths are nearly N-flat; rhombohedral widths grow with N, so absolute
thresholds transfer even worse across N). Trilayer-specific numbers in
this recipe (Lui's mixed-domain statistics, converter list) are N = 3
facts; treat the conversion direction — rhombohedral→Bernal only — as
the family-level rule. The mixed order ABCB is a two-way-FWHM blind spot
[citation, Wirth et al. arXiv:2203.07971 — not ingested]: FWHM alone may
not separate ABCB from ABAB (literature discriminates via G-peak
position and near-field imaging), so a Bernal-family FWHM call at N = 4
cannot exclude ABCB — hedge accordingly.

## Recipe

**Step 0 — inventory the data and its provenance (binding: produce the
table, not an acknowledgement).** For each file: excitation wavelength,
laser power, spot size, map step, spectral resolution/grating, raw vs
processed (background-subtracted? normalized?), acquisition date, and
**build stage** (what fabrication steps preceded the map; which followed
it, by risk class — metal deposition / transfer–pickup / chemical+bake /
clean thermal). Derived estimates satisfy the table when flagged as such
(spot size from objective NA, resolution from grating class); recorded
in-fiber power is not at-sample power — treat at-sample as unknown and
carry the conversion flag on the in-fiber value. Missing fields cap the
achievable strength: no wavelength
→ no lineshape comparison against references; no power → flag possible
in-measurement conversion if ≥ several mW; no stage → the call cannot be
mapped onto the finished device.

**Step 1 — layer count.** Establish N independently (optical contrast,
AFM, the supplier's characterization). If N is uncertain between 3 and 4,
the 2D read inherits that fork (Nguyen: ABC-3L vs ABC-4L needs blue
excitation) — report it, don't absorb it.

**Step 2 — per-spectrum 2D read.** Run the tool's metrics
(`raman_stacking/metrics.py`: single-Lorentzian FWHM, center, skew,
low/high ratio, fit r²) on every spectrum. Compare lineshapes against the
reference panels **at matching wavelength** (Lui Fig. 2; Nguyen Fig. 1).
Low r² with intermediate FWHM → mixed-spectrum candidate (Verify). Skew
and low/high ratio are secondary — their sign is excitation-dependent;
calibrate direction on the map's own populations, never assume it.

**Step 3 — map read (when a map exists).** Per-pixel metrics + junk-fit
rejection; **mask thickness populations before the split** (distinct
FWHM modes and amplitude steps belonging to other N) — a whole-map
split latches onto the thickness contrast and hides the stacking
bimodality. Then the two-population split
(`raman_stacking/map_tools.py`), trusted only where it is a population
structure (separation exceeding within-cluster spread, visible in the
histogram) — 2-means returns two clusters on any input, unimodal or
junk. Read the *morphology*: spatially
coherent clusters with sharp walls = domain pattern (strong); smooth
FWHM gradients tracking 2D-position shifts = strain field
(consistent-with strain, not ABC); population split co-locating with a
thickness terrace = layer-number artifact (uninformative for stacking).
Overlay spot/region coordinates on the flake image so the call is
spatially addressable downstream.

**Step 4 — cross-checks (as the data allows).** M-band region per
spectrum (red excitation preferred; away from the 2.1–2.4 eV crossing);
FWHM(G) map if G is covered; G-vs-2D position correlation to separate
strain from doping trends (citation, Lee NC 3 1024 — monolayer
calibration, use directionally). Where two independent channels agree on
a region, the verdict strengthens one grade; where they disagree, report
the conflict, not the average.

**Step 5 — stage-stamp the verdict.** From Step 0's build timeline:
verdict is "as of stage S". List post-map steps with their conversion
risk. Directionality: post-map processing can only have converted
ABC→ABA — a mapped-ABC region may be smaller/absent now; a mapped-ABA
region stays ABA (sub-spot ABC slivers and unmapped areas excepted).

**Step 6 — the call.** Output contract (all five parts mandatory):

1. Per-spot/per-region verdict on the strength scale (decisive / strong /
   weak / consistent-with / uninformative), each with its weight word and
   stage stamp: `region R (x,y µm, stage S): ABC (strong)`. Ship the
   region label mask/raster alongside the prose coordinates — fusion
   consumes the raster, and a prose-only region forces a lossy
   re-derivation downstream.
2. Evidence list: metric values with spectral coordinates (FWHM,
   population means, wavelength), the reference panel matched, map
   morphology, cross-check outcomes.
3. Confidence + named hedges: sub-spot blindness (domains below the spot
   size are invisible — this is structural, state it every time),
   wavelength coverage, resolution, unmapped areas, layer-count
   certainty.
4. What would firm it: second wavelength, M-band spectra, higher-res
   map, near-field imaging (s-SNOM resolves walls Raman cannot —
   citation, Kim ACS Nano 9 6765), or the transport check
   (`trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`).
5. **A reasoned "cannot tell" (with the missing metadata or coverage
   named) is a successful outcome. A confident call without
   feature-level evidence is a protocol violation.**

## Verify

- **Tool gates current.** `raman_stacking/validate.py` green (all gates;
  count and table in the tool README) before trusting metrics on new
  data; the gates double as the worked example of every metric.
- **Strain-mimic screen (mandatory before any ABC verdict from width
  alone).** Broad-FWHM region + smooth spatial gradient + correlated 2D
  position shift → consistent-with strain; broad region + bimodal
  population + sharp walls + stable 2D position → strong ABC. Uniaxial
  strain is the one confound that reproduces both broadening *and*
  asymmetry.
- **Through-stack screen (mandatory on any post-gate / mid-stack map).**
  From the build stage, list every graphene layer in the spot besides
  the target (graphite gates, contacts, adjacent flakes). A map taken
  **through a graphite gate is weak at best for the buried channel** —
  the collected 2D superposes the gate stack's Bernal-like band with the
  target's, and the per-spectrum metrics cannot unmix them; cap the
  verdict at consistent-with unless the gate contribution is modeled/
  subtracted or a pre-gate map exists (which then carries the call).
  [heuristic, QC0426 burn 2026-07-17: a post-fab map of a
  graphite-gated device read "uniform ABA (strong)" — PI review
  identified the signal as substantially the gate stack.]
- **Terrace screen.** Any candidate domain wall checked against the
  thickness map (optical/AFM); a wall coinciding with a layer step is
  uninformative for stacking. Without an external thickness map, in-map
  proxies can rule a terrace out: G/2D amplitudes — and the substrate
  line (e.g. Si 520 cm⁻¹) where unsaturated — step across a layer
  change and match across a stacking wall. **Check the proxy line is
  unclipped first**: a saturated line reads as a perfect match
  [heuristic, QC0426 flake map 2026-07-25 — Si line saturated, 2D
  amplitude carried the screen].
- **Twist screen (history-triggered only).** Run when the flake history
  suggests it — fold/tear/wrinkle near the region or a transfer anomaly;
  fabricated devices rarely warrant it. Trigger: moiré features or a 2D
  band decomposable as 1L+2L superposition → twist-contamination fork
  (citation, APL 118 133101): report, don't refine.
- **Mixed-spectrum decomposition.** For straddling candidates, run
  `raman_stacking/metrics.decompose_mixed` against the map's own
  population means; α in (0.2–0.8) (heuristic) → report as
  mixed/boundary, not as either stacking.
- **Excitation-transfer ban.** No threshold, reference lineshape, or
  skew direction crosses wavelengths; re-anchor on same-wavelength
  references or the map's own populations.
- **Absence claims cite resolvability.** "No ABC found" requires: map
  coverage stated, spot/step vs expected domain scale, power ≤ ~1 mW
  (else the measurement itself may have erased domains), pristine
  surface (processing broadening obscures contrast — Lui). Otherwise the
  outcome is "not resolved", not "absent".

## Examples

- QC0426 worked example (our-measurement,
  `hera/docs/notes/2026-07-17-QC0426-raman-fusion/raman-read/` + the
  correction in its README): a grower-supplied WITec project read
  end-to-end via `load_wip`. The read called uniform ABA (strong);
  **PI review identified the map as substantially probing the graphite
  gate stack** (post-fab device, graphite gates — Bernal-like 2D from
  the gates superposed on the channel's), and the verdict was downgraded
  to consistent-with — the burn that produced the through-stack screen
  (Verify). Mechanical lessons that stand: one of two scans proved
  partial *and* defocused (caught by Step 0 + per-pixel quality metrics);
  the single Spot spectrum landed on bare substrate (uninformative).
  Stage lesson: imagery-inferred stage stamps (both agents') were
  settled only by the grower — carry them as hedged inferences, never
  as established metadata.

- QC0426 pre-fab ladder (our-measurement,
  `hera/docs/notes/2026-07-25-QC0426-prefab-raman/`): maps of the same
  device at three build stages (flake / stack / finished device). Only
  the flake-stage map is gate-clean — graphite enters at the stack
  stage, so the through-stack screen triggers mid-ladder. Also the
  worked case for masking thickness populations before the split, the
  bimodality gate, and proxy-saturation checking (the flake map's Si
  line is clipped). Read details live in the note's contract.

- The FLG_37 mixed-flake map (labeled public data, 488 nm): per-pixel
  FWHM + two-population split resolved 60 vs 78 cm⁻¹ populations as
  spatially coherent domains with sharp walls; cluster means matched the
  deposit's labeled region averages to ~1 cm⁻¹
  (`hera/models/raman_stacking/README.md`, `flg37_map_validation.png`).
  Also the worked case for the layer-number discipline: the flake's 7-
  and 8-layer terraces carry distinct FWHM baselines.
- Metric calibration facts (which metrics are robust, which directions
  flip) live in the tool README's validation table — consult before
  weighting skew/ratio evidence.

## Next

- **Feeding fusion**: hand this contract's per-region verdicts to
  `stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md` for reconciliation with a
  transport call on the same device.
- **ABC-positive regions**: if the device/science depends on them,
  near-field imaging or the transport check before committing fridge
  time — Raman cannot see sub-spot structure or post-map conversion.
- **Ambiguous/strained/mixed**: the transport FS-count is the in-situ
  arbiter on the finished device; price it rather than re-arguing the
  same Raman data.

histogram) — 2-means returns two clusters on any input, unimodal or
junk. Read the *morphology*: spatially
coherent clusters with sharp walls = domain pattern (strong); smooth

thickness terrace = layer-number artifact (uninformative for stacking).

spatially addressable downstream.

spectrum (red excitation preferred; away from the 2.1–2.4 eV crossing);

strain from doping trends (citation, Lee NC 3 1024 — monolayer
calibration, use directionally). Where two independent channels agree on
a region, the verdict strengthens one grade; where they disagree, report
the conflict, not the average.

verdict is "as of stage S". List post-map steps with their conversion
risk. Directionality: post-map processing can only have converted

   population means, wavelength), the reference panel matched, map
   morphology, cross-check outcomes.

# Recipe style guide — epistemics for agent-executed science

*How to write recipes (especially `investigations/`) so that an agent
executing them literally is also executing them **calibratedly**. A recipe
is a program: an unstated validity condition is an unhandled branch, and
the agent will take it. Conservative rounding miscalibrates too — a rule
rounded toward caution makes the agent discard evidence it should weigh
(see burn log #1).*

## Rules

### 1. Rules carry their validity domain, inline

Never a bare binary ("X does not count", "X ⇒ Y"). The canonical form:

> **X alone is not evidence (because C); X together with Z is, weakening
> as W.**

The condition lives **at the rule**, in the same sentence or bullet — not
in a caveats appendix. Agents read locally; a caveat two sections away is
a caveat that doesn't execute.

### 2. Distinguish the three evidence axes

**Presence / pattern / magnitude.** Most miscalibration — in both
directions — comes from collapsing these:

- *presence*: the feature exists ("there are crossings")
- *pattern*: its structure matches a model ("a parallel-chain family
  co-locating with predicted ML×BL loci")
- *magnitude*: its size is in the predicted regime ("MΩ-insulating, not
  10 kΩ")

A rule about one axis must not be worded so it consumes the others
(burn log #1: a presence rule worded as a blanket rule discarded
pattern evidence).

### 3. Every discriminator names its confounds

For each "signal X ⇒ lean Y" rule, state what *else* produces X, next to
the rule. Standing examples in this corpus: series-path mosaic for
CNP-vs-D gap growth (any pair gaps if gappable domains span the channel);
two-domain beat fringes and grid aliasing for curved fan arcs. A
discriminator without a confounds list reads as stronger than it is.

### 4. Absence claims cite resolvability

"We did not see X" counts only with "and X was resolvable here because R"
— reference conditions (temperature, mobility/onset field, grid density)
against a stated benchmark. The resolution-ladder pattern
(`docs/papers/ncomms14518/paper.md#resolution-ladder`) is the house
implementation; replicate it for new investigations.

### 5. Provenance flags on factual claims

Mark each load-bearing claim as one of: **paper-data** (measured in the
cited reference), **citation** (claimed in the reference's citation
network, not its data), **our-measurement** (this lab, cite run ids),
**our-model** (this lab's validated forward model — cite the tool, and note
what gated it), **heuristic** (rule of thumb; state sample size — "n = 1
device" is common and fine, but say it). Unflagged claims read as paper-data.

### 6. Standardized strength vocabulary

Use exactly these words for evidence weight, and define calls with them:
**decisive · strong · weak · consistent-with · uninformative**. The
output contract should echo the same scale so calls are comparable
across sessions and recipes. "Supports", "suggests", "indicates" are
banned as load-bearing terms — they hide the weight.

### 7. Thresholds are labeled heuristics

Numeric triggers ("≥ 2 parallel chains", "rescale outside 0.8–1.2 is a
red flag") get a provenance flag (rule 5) and, where possible, the
failure mode they guard against. An unlabeled threshold gets treated as
physics.

### 8. "It depends" is a legal instruction

When a rule's condition is unmet, the recipe should say what *question*
to answer next, not force a branch. A decision ladder may bottom out in
"escalate to the operator with these specific alternatives" — that is an
outcome, not a gap.

### 9. Output contracts make hedging mandatory

Every investigation ends with a structured call: per-region/per-channel
verdicts, evidence list with coordinates and references, confidence with
named hedges, what-would-firm-it, and the explicit statement that a
reasoned "cannot tell" is success while an unevidenced confident call is
a protocol violation. (See `trilayer-stacking-id.md` step 5 for the
house form.)

### 10. Burn log — recipes are calibration instruments

When a rule misleads a live agent, fix the rule **and** record the burn
here, citing the session. Rules that have never been executed by an
agent are untested code.

### 11. Recipes are rig- and device-agnostic

Recipe steps contain **method** and **instrument-class conditionals**
("if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks,
then…") — never rig constants, driver names, or device numbers. The rig
prompt, device card, and session brief supply the parameters that
resolve the conditionals. Device- or rig-specific numbers are allowed
only in Examples, provenance-tagged (rule 5) — **except operating
setpoints** (gate operating points, screening voltages): those are
calibration data; Examples cite where the value is recorded
(`measurement_config`, notebook index, device card), never quote it.
An operational default quoted in an agent-visible file becomes an
inherited choice (burn log #5). Test: *could this recipe run on a
different fridge with only the device card and brief swapped?*

**Variant layer**: when instrument-class conditionals can't carry the
rig's reality — the rig changes the *procedure's shape*, not just its
parameters (e.g. a gate source with no leakage readback forces a
repatch workflow) — write a rig **variant** (`<base>-<rig>.md`, rule
13) instead of bloating the base with rig prose. Line test:
*parameters* change → conditional in the base; *procedure shape*
changes → variant file. Device-specific content (a particular flake's
numbers or wiring) never becomes a recipe at all — that lives in the
device card and `templates/<device>/`.

### 12. Feasibility-first: design-time guards beat post-hoc verification

**Feasibility-first** is the general tenet, and it governs *every*
measurement: before committing fridge time — especially to a long sweep —
work out **(1)** the **expected signature** (the specific feature:
frequency, gap, peak position, magnitude), **(2)** whether it is
**resolvable** on this apparatus (field / temperature / sensitivity
envelope), and **(3)** the **data density** needed to see it (field steps,
oscillation periods, 1/B record length, n-spacing). *Only then* spend the
time. Investigations **reference this rule** rather than restating it; where
the discriminator is a small signal, the feasibility pass is load-bearing,
not a formality (worked example: the FS-count Step 2,
`investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`).

The sampling corner of this is mandatory and concrete:
Sampling/Nyquist checks (every swept axis), dynamic-range checks, and
the full cost model belong at **sweep-design time**. Verify-section
robustness tests confirm a sound design; they cannot rescue an
undersampled one — a fan that fails Nyquist in the claim window is
uninformative there, re-measure. Corollary: timing/overhead constants
are **calibrated from the session's own early sweeps**, not inherited;
an uncalibrated constant in a brief is a bug with false authority, and
the agent should treat it as a prior to check, not a fact.
**Extension to briefs**: every logistics number in a session brief
carries an honesty marker — `[measured: run N, date]` or `[assumed]` —
so the agent knows which figures are priors to re-derive (burn log #2).
**Settling floor**: a swept-point dwell has a floor near the
lock-in/filter time constant (`dwell ≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at
24 dB/oct) — below it the reading lags the true value. Derive the dwell
from the *measured* τ by default (read it before pricing; bring-up
records it so it lands in metadata) rather than a round number — the
same discipline as not inheriting a timing constant. The floor can be
bent judiciously — only when the lag is benign for the quantity
extracted: a uniform lag merely offsets a *read*-axis slope-fit's
intercept, and a smooth high-SNR signal tolerates some — but on a *fast*
axis feeding a per-column transform (a fan's FFT) it suppresses the
high-frequency tones. What's not OK is an *unexamined* round-number dwell
on an unknown τ. (burn log #6, #8)

### 13. Variants declare base, deltas, reasons, obsolescence

A rig variant opens by naming its **base recipe** and listing exactly
which steps it overrides, each with the **rig fact that forces the
override** ("DC205 has no leakage readback ⇒ step 2 becomes the
repatch workflow"). It never restates base content it doesn't change —
readers hold base + deltas, not two diverging copies. It ends with its
**obsolescence condition**: the hardware/driver change that would
delete it (e.g. a switch matrix obsoletes a repatch idiom) — variants
are workarounds with an expiry, not permanent forks. On their rig,
variants take precedence over their base (rig prompts encode this).

### 14. Extraction-sensitive claims are forks, not refinement targets

When a quantitative claim **flips under extraction-parameter changes**
(window, detrend order, fit range, threshold), stop refining and report
the **fork**: the robust finding, the parameter-dependent finding, and
the **deciding measurement** that would resolve it. A third extraction
scheme is not evidence — it's a third vote in an electorate you
invented. Separate what survives all reasonable parameter choices from
what doesn't, and price the measurement that settles it.

### 16. Load-bearing steps produce an output, not advice

An instruction an agent can satisfy by *acknowledging* it — "estimate the
cost", "consider the worst corner", "flag it to the operator" — is an escape
hatch, and under token pressure the agent takes it. A check that must hold:

- **Binding, not advisory** — demand a required artifact ("compute `N_B`,
  `N_n`, wall-clock; propose exactly one design"), not "estimate / consider /
  flag".
- **Computed, not eyeballed** — if a function yields the quantity, call it
  (`B_lo = sdh_onset(...)`); eyeballed quantities run biased and high-variance.
- **Forceful — keep the forcing** — the "do X, *not* Y, because Y fails"
  warning is the mechanism, not padding; trimming it to a bare formula re-opens
  the escape. (This rule fights the terse instinct: for a binding gate the
  forcing clause earns its tokens.)

twice: the out-of-window record is lost outright, and — because record
quality (tone separation, δF, onset) improves with range — the
*in-window* claim degrades too. Cost is the legitimate cap ("range past
what the claim needs is just cost"); "the model can't interpret there"
is not. Test: would the extra range improve the measured record for the
in-window claim, at acceptable cost? Then take it, and flag the
overlay's domain in the read. (burn log #9)

1. **2026-06-11, QC0426 live session** (`trilayer-stacking-id`): the
   step-4 rule "crossings at finite D no longer count as ABA evidence"
   — written conservatively to prevent overconfidence — caused HERA to
   discard the chain hunt at D = +0.25 entirely ("this run informs gap
   physics, not the chain hunt"). The physics: crossing *presence* at
   finite D is indeed not ABA evidence (Lee et al.), but a chain
   *pattern* matching the ML×BL model loci still is, weakening with
   |D|. Fixed by restating per rules 1–2. Lesson: rounding a
   conditional rule toward caution miscalibrates exactly as badly as
   rounding it toward confidence.

2. **2026-06-10/11, QC0426 live session** (`landau-fan` +
   session brief): iteration-1 fan was B-axis aliased (0.25 T rows vs
   ~0.29 T in-window SdH period) — blocky texture, arc evidence
   discounted; recovered by the overnight 0.05 T fan. Failure chain
   spanned three documents: the brief carried a toploader-derived
   "~30 s/row" (measured: 278 s/row, ramp-limited on a blocking
   magnet), the agent sized a coarse-B fan to the mispriced budget, and
   no design-time Nyquist guard existed to catch it. Fixed by the
   landau-fan grid-design check + full cost model and rules 11–12.
   Lesson: a wrong constant with false authority plus a missing design
   guard compound; agnostic recipes with instrument-class conditionals
   force the agent to resolve parameters against the actual rig.

3. **2026-06-10, QC0426 live session** (run-5 SdH-FFT analysis): three
   successive f_low-extraction schemes gave conflicting slope signs
   before the agent stepped back and separated robust findings (two
   frequency scales, f₁+f₂=f_tot) from window-dependent ones (f_low's
   n-dependence). The agent self-diagnosed the spiral in its session
   notes; rule 14 canonizes its own lesson. Lesson: refinement loops on
   extraction-sensitive quantities consume session time and manufacture
   confidence — the fork report + deciding measurement is the correct
   terminal state.

4. **2026-06-10/11, QC0426 live session** (`trilayer-stacking-id`,
   post-mortem 06-12): run-4's vertical candidate came from a 4-row /
   0.25 T window — a dispersing minimum (true slope-ν ≈ 5.1 at fine
   rows) read as "non-dispersing". No rule barred a dispersion claim
   from a window that cannot resolve dispersion; the session
   adjudicated it correctly (anomaly, not evidence) but retiring the
   candidate cost a queued measurement. Fixed by the step-3 dispersion
   floor (≥ ~8 B-rows spanning ≥ 1.5 T, else "dispersion
   undetermined"). Lesson: a classifier without a stated resolution
   floor manufactures candidates from coarse data.

# Tetralayer stacking identification by Fermi-surface counting (ABAB / ABCA / ABCB)

*Investigation — a decision procedure one level up from the measurement recipes
it orchestrates (`measurements/gatemap.md`, `measurements/sdh-spot-check.md`,
`measurements/landau-fan.md`), spanning multiple measurements rather than a single
sweep. Use the rig-appropriate variants; rig and device mechanics — magnet
discipline, gate wiring, validators — live in the device card and session brief,
not here. Trilayer devices use the sibling `trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`; the
device card's material line routes.*

**Reference**: `hera/docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md` — the survey
that grounds this recipe, synthesising Min–MacDonald 2008
(`hera/docs/papers/0711.4333/paper.md`), Koshino–McCann 2011
(`hera/docs/papers/1104.0794/paper.md`), Grushina et al. 2015
(`hera/docs/papers/1501.06764/paper.md`), and Kalantre et al. 2026
(`hera/docs/papers/2606.05356/paper.md`). Read it first; every band-structure
claim below is grounded there.

## What

Classify the stacking order of a tetralayer-graphene device — ABAB (Bernal),
ABCA (rhombohedral), or ABCB (mixed) — by **counting distinct Fermi surfaces**
from Shubnikov–de Haas frequency content at controlled D ≈ 0, read as a peak
set against the Luttinger frequency. Output is a **region-resolved,
evidence-cited, hedged call**, not a headline.

## When

- A **dual-gated** tetralayer device of unknown or unverified stacking is loaded
  and gated, where you can sit at D = 0 and sweep n independently. (No
  single-gated tetralayer procedure exists in the corpus — a single-gated 4L
  device is an uncovered case to flag, not to improvise.)
- Stacking determines everything downstream (ABCA hosts the flat-band /
  correlated / superconducting physics; ABAB is conventional; ABCB is a
  metastable gapped oddity), so this is typically among the *first science
  questions* of a tetralayer campaign.
- Also worth running when stacking was assigned optically / by Raman only —
  transport is the in-situ check, and exfoliated multilayer flakes commonly
  host **mixed stacking domains**, so different contact pairs can disagree.
  (Raman side: `raman-stacking-id.md`; reconciling: `stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md`.)

Prerequisites: gates calibrated with validators committed (device-init
recipes), and at least one four-terminal Rxx channel with credible contacts and
quantum mobility high enough to reach SdH onset in the planned field window
(Step 3 decides this). Step 1 handles CNP identification and the (n, D)
conversion — a CNP that cannot be positively identified is itself an outcome to
surface, not a precondition.

## Why

The three stackings differ in Fermi-surface count *and* in where their tones
sit (`hera/docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md` §1–2):

- **ABAB**: two bilayer-like parabolic bands (effective interlayer couplings
  1.618γ₁ / 0.618γ₁) coexist → **2 Fermi surfaces**, densities partitioning
  ∝ mass.
- **ABCA**: a single chiral J = 4 quartic band with trigonal-warping Lifshitz
  structure confined to low density → **1 Fermi surface** at the ~10¹²
  operating density.
- **ABCB**: a cubic band plus a Dirac-like band over an intrinsic ~9 meV CNP
  gap → **2 Fermi surfaces** with a light, velocity-renormalized Dirac partner
  (citation-grade — no validated model backs quantitative ABCB reads).

**The read is the peak set against the Luttinger frequency.** F_L = (h/4e)·n
(g = 4, spin × valley, unbroken at the operating point — Verify: degeneracy
audit) is the predicted line, inheriting the lever-arm **scale** uncertainty
(geometry prior ~10–15% — `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md`), so F_L
is a **band, not a ceiling**. The templates:

- **ABCA**: one tone **at** F_L (the single pocket carries the full density).
- **ABAB**: a **pair** partitioning F_L at ≈ **0.72 / 0.28** (the φ² mass
  ratio; decomposition-limit values — the model's F(n) table is the design
  authority). Two exception regimes [our-model]: at low *electron* density
  the light pocket nearly empties and the heavy tone rides at ≈ 0.95·F_L —
  where ABAB genuinely mimics an ABCA singleton within the scale prior —
  and the near-CNP *hole* pair is close and balanced (beat-like on short
  1/B records). Both wash out by |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹².
- **ABCB**: a pair partitioning F_L with a *light Dirac* partner — a
  shape-discriminated variant of the two-tone case (citation-grade).
- **Mixed stacking domains**: templates superposed, each grouping checked
  against the **same** F_L (domains share the gated density). Peak
  *amplitudes* track the domains' geometric weighting.
- **A tone at F_L is not automatically ABCA**: an ABAB pair sums to F_L, so a
  **magnetic breakdown** orbit through both pockets or an intermodulation tone
  lands exactly at F_L and mimics the ABCA singleton — and unlike the trilayer
  case, ABAB inter-block breakdown is **symmetry-allowed** (no parity
  protection between the two bilayer-like blocks), so treat the sum-tone
  confound as *expected*, not exotic. A set {f₁, f₂, ≈F_L} underdetermines
  mixed domains; discriminate before claiming one (Verify: F_L-tone origin —
  mandatory for any singleton call where partner tones are resolved).

Against the trilayer read, this one is structurally **easier at design
densities |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹²**: the dominant tones themselves separate (ABAB's
biggest tone at ≈ 0.72–0.79·F_L vs ABCA's at F_L), and the ABAB partner tone
carries ~21–28% of F_L rather than a few percent. The discriminating
evidence is the dominant-tone *position* plus the partition — not a
small-tone hunt. The advantage evaporates in the low-|n| exception regimes
above — design around them (Step 2).

Four disciplines keep it honest (unchanged from the trilayer method; stated
here because this recipe runs standalone):

- **Pin the scale before you reject.** The lever arm is one global number the
  Luttinger relations pin — a singleton sits at F_L, a pair sums to F_L. Fit
  that single in-band scale to the *whole* peak set first; a peak is "above
  F_L" only after the scale is pinned. Multiple populations (mixed domains)
  over-determine the scale — leverage, not noise. Any later scale change is
  retroactive — re-read the whole set.
- **Classify on frequencies, never amplitudes.** Amplitudes fold in field,
  Dingle damping, and domain weighting; frequencies carry the pocket areas.
- **Screen harmonics first — and Luttinger-aware.** Drop any peak at an
  integer multiple of a stronger fundamental (confirm by n-dependence — a
  harmonic tracks k·f exactly; a real pocket follows its own Onsager curve),
  but never discard a tone as a harmonic when doing so breaks the partition
  sum: the ABAB pair's ratio ≈ 2.6 drifts through 3× with density, and a
  ratio-only screen eats the real heavy tone exactly there [our-model,
  synthetic replay]. The n-dependence screen plus the sum decide, not the
  ratio alone.
- **Read each Rxx channel separately, never averaged.** Each pair probes a
  region of a possibly-mosaic flake; the call is **per region**, and "most
  channels uninformative" is a normal outcome.

Two design facts:

- **D ≈ 0 is the operating point.** Finite D gaps ABCA, reshapes ABAB's
  overlap and hybridizes its blocks, and splits ABAB valleys. A quantitative
  small-residual-D robustness statement is pending the model — treat residual
  D as "keep it small," a heuristic, not a guarantee (survey §3).
- **No side prior.** Both signs get a spot check (Step 3); the fan follows the
  cleaner side.

## Recipe

**Step 0 — mine what's already on disk.** An existing D = 0 fan with adequate
low-field reach already answers most of this via per-column FFT (Step 4);
existing 0 T gate maps answer Step 1.

**Step 1 — B = 0 (n, D) gate map + the (n, D) conversion.** As in the trilayer
sibling, verbatim: calibration from `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md`
(ratio data-calibrated, scale geometry-prior); identify clean hole- and
electron-side regions and the D = 0 line; flag arms going insulating; pick
voltage pairs metallic across the planned n-range. One tetralayer addendum: an
insulating CNP at D ≈ 0 is **not** a stacking read — it has three candidate
parents (ABCB intrinsic gap; ABCA under residual D; interaction-gapped ABAB in
ultraclean devices) — record it and move on (survey §5).

**Step 2 — feasibility (binding: compute, don't eyeball).** The reference
frequency is **F_L = (h/4e)·n**. From it and the template partitions, compute
the three design numbers before any sweep:

- **Δ(1/B) resolution** — Nyquist on F_L (the fastest expected tone):
  Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L).
- **Tone separation** — the binding resolution case is separating the ABAB
  heavy tone from an ABCA singleton (F_L), and resolving the ABAB partner
  with ≥ ~5 periods: (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi) ≥ 5/f_partner. Take both tones'
  frequencies from the **model's F(n) table**
  (`hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count/`), not the bare 0.72/0.28 ratios — and
  pick design densities |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹² where the templates separate: at
  +1×10¹² the ABAB heavy tone sits within ~5% of F_L and the partner at
  ~0.6 T is unresolvable in any practical window [our-model].
- **The field window** — onset is measured in Step 3, not computed; keep the
  ~100 mT-scale heuristic as an expectation only.

**Step 3 — SdH spot checks (`sdh-spot-check.md`).** Two spot checks — large
hole and large electron density (push |n| high within gate limits and any
contact-stress ceiling) — each fixed-(n, D = 0), uniform in 1/B, Δ(1/B) from
Step 2. From each FFT: which tones are present, and which side is cleaner. A
clean spot check can be **decisive on its own**; lock its sampling, settling,
and sensitivity and hand them, with the measured onset, to Step 4.

**Step 4 — full Landau fan + per-column FFT (`landau-fan.md`).** Fan on the
cleaner side over a decently large density window at D = 0. Field range from
Step 3 (onset → B_lo; period-count extrapolation to the low-density edge sets
B_hi — the ABAB partner tone at the lowest fan density is the binding case).
Inherit the spot check's Δ(1/B) and settling. FFT each n-column; read peak set
vs F_L, the Luttinger partition, and each tone's n-dependence in one object.

**Step 5 — F(n) across density (the refinement).** (1) **Partition
robustness** — f₁(n) + f₂(n) = F_L(n) across density is algebraic (no model);
a coincidental one-density match will not hold. (2) **Branch labeling** —
overlay measured F(n) on the model curves (Verify: forward-model comparison):
ABAB branches are *both parabolic* and are labeled by the frequency ratio and
per-branch mass (Verify: LK), **not** by shape; a light *Dirac-shaped* branch
(supra-linear F(n) at low n against the model) points at ABCB's J = 1 partner
[citation-grade — report as candidate, hedge accordingly]. The binary
ABAB-pair vs ABCA-singleton call needs only (1) plus the F_L-tone origin
discrimination.

**Step 6 — high field (weak complement only).** There is **no tetralayer
Streda/Chern offset discriminator**: every 4L stacking carries 16 zero-energy
LLs — a ν = ±8, 12, 16 low-field ladder confirms the *layer number*, not the
stacking (survey §4; the layer-number check is itself useful — Verify:
adjacent-N). Stacking-dependent LL *fine structure* (two interleaved bilayer
ladders with mod-3 anticrossings vs a single bunched ladder) is qualitative —
no validated 4L LL model — so weight anything from it ≤ weak.

**Step 7 — the call.** Output contract (all five parts mandatory):

1. Per-region verdict on the STYLE strength scale: `channel/pair X: ABAB
   (strong) | ABCA (weak) | ABCB-candidate (consistent-with) | mixed-domain
   (consistent-with) | uninformative` — every verdict carries its weight word;
   bare leans are not verdicts.
2. Evidence list: each tone claimed, with frequency, (n, D) coordinates and
   density side, the Onsager-overlay artifact, and the Luttinger check.
3. Confidence + specific hedges (resolution limits, side/density, features
   searched-and-absent vs not-resolvable, domain/mosaic caveat, **absolute
   layer number** — if the peak set matches neither 4L template, the
   adjacent-N hypothesis belongs here before exotic explanations).
4. What would firm the call (other side, LK mass split, degeneracy audit,
   independent N-ID, a different rig/temperature).
5. **A "cannot tell" with reasons is a successful outcome. A confident call
   without feature-level evidence is a protocol violation.**

## Verify

- **TSV-first is mandatory for any classification-grade read.** Re-form
  Rxx(n, B) at native grid resolution (channel arithmetic per the device card)
  before any frequency claim; rendered monitor PNGs alias the SdH structure.

indexes, never here — STYLE rule 11.)*

# Tetralayer stacking identification by Fermi-surface counting (ABAB / ABCA / ABCB)

*Investigation — a decision procedure one level up from the measurement recipes
it orchestrates (`measurements/gatemap.md`, `measurements/sdh-spot-check.md`,
`measurements/landau-fan.md`), spanning multiple measurements rather than a single
sweep. Use the rig-appropriate variants; rig and device mechanics — magnet
discipline, gate wiring, validators — live in the device card and session brief,
not here. Trilayer devices use the sibling `trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`; the
device card's material line routes.*

**Reference**: `hera/docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md` — the survey
that grounds this recipe, synthesising Min–MacDonald 2008
(`hera/docs/papers/0711.4333/paper.md`), Koshino–McCann 2011
(`hera/docs/papers/1104.0794/paper.md`), Grushina et al. 2015
(`hera/docs/papers/1501.06764/paper.md`), and Kalantre et al. 2026
(`hera/docs/papers/2606.05356/paper.md`). Read it first; every band-structure
claim below is grounded there.

## What

Classify the stacking order of a tetralayer-graphene device — ABAB (Bernal),
ABCA (rhombohedral), or ABCB (mixed) — by **counting distinct Fermi surfaces**
from Shubnikov–de Haas frequency content at controlled D ≈ 0, read as a peak
set against the Luttinger frequency. Output is a **region-resolved,
evidence-cited, hedged call**, not a headline.

## When

- A **dual-gated** tetralayer device of unknown or unverified stacking is loaded
  and gated, where you can sit at D = 0 and sweep n independently. (No
  single-gated tetralayer procedure exists in the corpus — a single-gated 4L
  device is an uncovered case to flag, not to improvise.)
- Stacking determines everything downstream (ABCA hosts the flat-band /
  correlated / superconducting physics; ABAB is conventional; ABCB is a
  metastable gapped oddity), so this is typically among the *first science
  questions* of a tetralayer campaign.
- Also worth running when stacking was assigned optically / by Raman only —
  transport is the in-situ check, and exfoliated multilayer flakes commonly
  host **mixed stacking domains**, so different contact pairs can disagree.
  (Raman side: `raman-stacking-id.md`; reconciling: `stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md`.)

Prerequisites: gates calibrated with validators committed (device-init
recipes), and at least one four-terminal Rxx channel with credible contacts and
quantum mobility high enough to reach SdH onset in the planned field window
(Step 3 decides this). Step 1 handles CNP identification and the (n, D)
conversion — a CNP that cannot be positively identified is itself an outcome to
surface, not a precondition.

## Why

The three stackings differ in Fermi-surface count *and* in where their tones
sit (`hera/docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md` §1–2):

- **ABAB**: two bilayer-like parabolic bands (effective interlayer couplings
  1.618γ₁ / 0.618γ₁) coexist → **2 Fermi surfaces**, densities partitioning
  ∝ mass.
- **ABCA**: a single chiral J = 4 quartic band with trigonal-warping Lifshitz
  structure confined to low density → **1 Fermi surface** at the ~10¹²
  operating density.
- **ABCB**: a cubic band plus a Dirac-like band over an intrinsic ~9 meV CNP
  gap → **2 Fermi surfaces** with a light, velocity-renormalized Dirac partner
  (citation-grade — no validated model backs quantitative ABCB reads).

**The read is the peak set against the Luttinger frequency.** F_L = (h/4e)·n
(g = 4, spin × valley, unbroken at the operating point — Verify: degeneracy
audit) is the predicted line, inheriting the lever-arm **scale** uncertainty
(geometry prior ~10–15% — `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md`), so F_L
is a **band, not a ceiling**. The templates:

- **ABCA**: one tone **at** F_L (the single pocket carries the full density).
- **ABAB**: a **pair** partitioning F_L at ≈ **0.72 / 0.28** (the φ² mass
  ratio; decomposition-limit values — the model's F(n) table is the design
  authority). Two exception regimes [our-model]: at low *electron* density
  the light pocket nearly empties and the heavy tone rides at ≈ 0.95·F_L —
  where ABAB genuinely mimics an ABCA singleton within the scale prior —
  and the near-CNP *hole* pair is close and balanced (beat-like on short
  1/B records). Both wash out by |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹².
- **ABCB**: a pair partitioning F_L with a *light Dirac* partner — a
  shape-discriminated variant of the two-tone case (citation-grade).
- **Mixed stacking domains**: templates superposed, each grouping checked
  against the **same** F_L (domains share the gated density). Peak
  *amplitudes* track the domains' geometric weighting.
- **A tone at F_L is not automatically ABCA**: an ABAB pair sums to F_L, so a
  **magnetic breakdown** orbit through both pockets or an intermodulation tone
  lands exactly at F_L and mimics the ABCA singleton — and unlike the trilayer
  case, ABAB inter-block breakdown is **symmetry-allowed** (no parity
  protection between the two bilayer-like blocks), so treat the sum-tone
  confound as *expected*, not exotic. A set {f₁, f₂, ≈F_L} underdetermines
  mixed domains; discriminate before claiming one (Verify: F_L-tone origin —
  mandatory for any singleton call where partner tones are resolved).

Against the trilayer read, this one is structurally **easier at design
densities |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹²**: the dominant tones themselves separate (ABAB's
biggest tone at ≈ 0.72–0.79·F_L vs ABCA's at F_L), and the ABAB partner tone
carries ~21–28% of F_L rather than a few percent. The discriminating
evidence is the dominant-tone *position* plus the partition — not a
small-tone hunt. The advantage evaporates in the low-|n| exception regimes
above — design around them (Step 2).

Four disciplines keep it honest (unchanged from the trilayer method; stated
here because this recipe runs standalone):

- **Pin the scale before you reject.** The lever arm is one global number the
  Luttinger relations pin — a singleton sits at F_L, a pair sums to F_L. Fit
  that single in-band scale to the *whole* peak set first; a peak is "above
  F_L" only after the scale is pinned. Multiple populations (mixed domains)
  over-determine the scale — leverage, not noise. Any later scale change is
  retroactive — re-read the whole set.
- **Classify on frequencies, never amplitudes.** Amplitudes fold in field,
  Dingle damping, and domain weighting; frequencies carry the pocket areas.
- **Screen harmonics first — and Luttinger-aware.** Drop any peak at an
  integer multiple of a stronger fundamental (confirm by n-dependence — a
  harmonic tracks k·f exactly; a real pocket follows its own Onsager curve),
  but never discard a tone as a harmonic when doing so breaks the partition
  sum: the ABAB pair's ratio ≈ 2.6 drifts through 3× with density, and a
  ratio-only screen eats the real heavy tone exactly there [our-model,
  synthetic replay]. The n-dependence screen plus the sum decide, not the
  ratio alone.
- **Read each Rxx channel separately, never averaged.** Each pair probes a
  region of a possibly-mosaic flake; the call is **per region**, and "most
  channels uninformative" is a normal outcome.

Two design facts:

- **D ≈ 0 is the operating point.** Finite D gaps ABCA, reshapes ABAB's
  overlap and hybridizes its blocks, and splits ABAB valleys. A quantitative
  small-residual-D robustness statement is pending the model — treat residual
  D as "keep it small," a heuristic, not a guarantee (survey §3).
- **No side prior.** Both signs get a spot check (Step 3); the fan follows the
  cleaner side.

**Step 0 — mine what's already on disk.** An existing D = 0 fan with adequate
low-field reach already answers most of this via per-column FFT (Step 4);
existing 0 T gate maps answer Step 1.

**Step 1 — B = 0 (n, D) gate map + the (n, D) conversion.** As in the trilayer
sibling, verbatim: calibration from `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md`

electron-side regions and the D = 0 line; flag arms going insulating; pick
voltage pairs metallic across the planned n-range. One tetralayer addendum: an
insulating CNP at D ≈ 0 is **not** a stacking read — it has three candidate
parents (ABCB intrinsic gap; ABCA under residual D; interaction-gapped ABAB in
ultraclean devices) — record it and move on (survey §5).

**Step 2 — feasibility (binding: compute, don't eyeball).** The reference
frequency is **F_L = (h/4e)·n**. From it and the template partitions, compute
the three design numbers before any sweep:

- **Δ(1/B) resolution** — Nyquist on F_L (the fastest expected tone):
  Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L).
- **Tone separation** — the binding resolution case is separating the ABAB
  heavy tone from an ABCA singleton (F_L), and resolving the ABAB partner
  with ≥ ~5 periods: (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi) ≥ 5/f_partner. Take both tones'
  frequencies from the **model's F(n) table**
  (`hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count/`), not the bare 0.72/0.28 ratios — and
  pick design densities |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹² where the templates separate: at
  +1×10¹² the ABAB heavy tone sits within ~5% of F_L and the partner at
  ~0.6 T is unresolvable in any practical window [our-model].
- **The field window** — onset is measured in Step 3, not computed; keep the
  ~100 mT-scale heuristic as an expectation only.

**Step 3 — SdH spot checks (`sdh-spot-check.md`).** Two spot checks — large
hole and large electron density (push |n| high within gate limits and any
contact-stress ceiling) — each fixed-(n, D = 0), uniform in 1/B, Δ(1/B) from
Step 2. From each FFT: which tones are present, and which side is cleaner. A
clean spot check can be **decisive on its own**; lock its sampling, settling,
and sensitivity and hand them, with the measured onset, to Step 4.

**Step 4 — full Landau fan + per-column FFT (`landau-fan.md`).** Fan on the
cleaner side over a decently large density window at D = 0. Field range from

Inherit the spot check's Δ(1/B) and settling. FFT each n-column; read peak set

**Step 5 — F(n) across density (the refinement).** (1) **Partition

2. Evidence list: each tone claimed, with frequency, (n, D) coordinates and

4. What would firm the call (other side, LK mass split, degeneracy audit,

5. **A "cannot tell" with reasons is a successful outcome. A confident call

*(No live tetralayer sessions yet — this section seeds from the first

indexes, never here — STYLE rule 11.)*

  magnet time.

24 dB/oct. STYLE rule 12's settling floor (k ≈ 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) puts a
settled point at ~2–3 s, ~10x the rig card's "standard fp set ≈ 0.2–0.25 s/pt
at NPLC=1". Whatever run calibrated that 0.2–0.25 s figure must have been at a
much shorter tau, but the rig card's Timing section does not say so, and run
metadata stores tau as `None` — so the number reads as universal when it is
not. Suggest the rig card's per-point figure carry the tau/slope it was
measured at. Measuring the actual cost at Gate C before pricing anything long.

exec 16 — continues the operator's [1]-[15] sequence, all 9 instruments
registered). VERIFY `ALL GREEN` (cell 33, exec 17). Reading the extra grant as
covering lock-in sensitivity / time-constant / filter-slope / oscillator
amplitude only: the session-banned safety surfaces stay banned regardless, and
the specifically consent-gated knobs (`dc205.ramp_rate`, Keithley `volt.step`,
`set_both` ratio) still get a specific ask — a blanket phrase is not an
affirmative go on a specific proposal.

re-run as cell 39.** It sampled `sr1.X` 24 times back-to-back, ~0.7 s of wall
clock, and reported the std as per-point noise. At tau = 0.3 s those samples are
correlated (roughly two independent values), so the std was biased *low* for
large tau and the comparison was rigged toward the setting I already suspected
was right — it printed a fake 80x noise cliff between tau=0.3 and tau=0.1.
Sampling at the dwell interval instead gave 0.79% vs 1.73%, a factor of 2.2,
close to the sqrt(3) white-noise expectation. Generalisable lesson worth putting
somewhere agents will read it: **any lock-in noise measurement must sample at
>= the filter correlation time**, and the natural choice is the dwell the sweep
will actually use. A settling/noise characterisation helper in `hera.analysis`
that enforces this would stop the next agent making the same mistake.
