It says "HERA proposes Cell A and Cell B together, and does not propose any
subsequent recipe step until the human reports the per-leg results... Human is
the gate; HERA waits." Under an E1 grant there is no human keystroke per leg and
the agent reads the four run directories off disk itself, which is a stronger
check than eyeballing the live plot. Ran it that way. The section needs an E1
branch, or the handshake language needs to move to a mode-conditional note —
otherwise a literal-minded agent under E1 either stalls forever or silently
violates the recipe.

**RECIPE FIX — gate-current-sanity-check.md Cell A carries toploader-isms.** Its
code block uses `sr830_1..4` and `measurement_config`, while this rig's notebooks
bind `sr0..sr3` and `meas_config`; it also hardcodes `delay = 1` and
`n_pts = 251` with no note that the delay should be the rig/session settling
floor rather than a default. Used dwell = 0.70 s (this session's measured 7*tau)
and 151 pts, stated on the page.

**TOOLING — no Hall-bar geometry (L/W) on the device card.** R_xx reads 206 ohm
at (0,0) but without the B_1-B_2 aspect ratio that cannot be turned into a sheet
resistance, so it cannot be turned into an n*mu estimate either — which is
exactly the number needed to guess whether the CNP sits inside the committed
gate window before spending 20 minutes finding out. Worth a geometry line on
device cards for dual-gated Hall bars.

**PROTOCOL — priced the gate map 2x too high by transferring a per-point cost
across sweep types.** Gate C's 1D legs ran 1.79 s/pt; I subtracted an estimated
0.30 s for the nplci 10->1 change and quoted 1.49 s/pt for the megasweep, ETA
1h45m. Actual: 0.87 s/pt, 69 rows/min, ETA 53 min. The 1D legs carried a parked-
gate `volt` read and `nplci = 10` that the megasweep does not, and megasweep's
per-point path is leaner than `sweep`'s. Lesson: a measured s/pt calibrates the
*sweep type and fp set it was measured on*; re-derive rather than adjust when
either changes. Over-pricing is the safe direction but it distorts planning.

**TOOLING — hera-watch LEAK warning fires on common-mode pickup.** Gate map run
4 row 0 raised `LEAK k_2400_tg=D203pA`. The underlying trend is a real ~65 pA
leakage onset above V_tg ~ 0.5 V, but the 203 pA figure comes from ~3 isolated
points where I_tg AND I_bg jump *together with the same sign* - common-mode
pickup, not leakage (a TG-BG leak is equal and opposite; a leak to ground shows
on one gate only). Suggest the warning test the differential (I_tg + I_bg, or
correlation between gate channels) before flagging, or at least report both
gates' excursions side by side so the common-mode case is visible from the
digest without going to the TSV.

**DEVICE — top-gate leakage onset at V_tg ~ 0.5-0.62 V, ~65-88 pA at +1.0 V.**
Seen in Gate C run 0 (flat -97 pA to 0.62 V, then up to -10 pA at +1.0 V) and
reproduced in gate map run 4 row 0 at V_bg = -1.3 (flat -100 pA to ~0.5 V, then
~-35 pA above 0.6 V). TG-positive only; TG-negative and both BG polarities flat.
Below the 1 nA abort. Operator notified; running to the committed +1.0 V because
capping at 0.6 V costs the electron-side density the investigation needs
(n_max 3.3e12 -> 1.9e12). `gate-leakage-survey` is blocklisted so this is
recorded, not characterised - it belongs in the device card for the next session.

**PROTOCOL — a ridge tracker seeded on a prior slope produced a confident,
wrong, high-sigma result.** Gate map run 4. My first tracker walked every row
predicting each ridge's position from the geometry-prior slope and taking the
nearest peak. Where ridge A had not yet appeared it happily matched ridge B's
peak to ridge A, producing a spliced track and the report "|dA-dB| = 0.38,
23.7 sigma -> NOT parallel". The tell was in the same printout: 24 mV rms
residual on the spliced track vs 2.4 mV on the clean one. Two lessons worth
landing in the corpus: (1) **never seed a feature tracker with the quantity you
are trying to measure** - continuity from a known row with mutual exclusion is
the right shape; (2) a sigma value should not be printed without its residuals
next to it, and `cnp-and-dline-calibration` Step 2 should say so explicitly (it
says "report slope and intercept per channel with fit residuals" but does not
warn that the residual is the *tracker* diagnostic, not just the fit quality).

**RECIPE FIX — cnp-and-dline-calibration assumes the ridge IS a CNP line.**
Its Step 1-3 go straight from "locate the Rxx maximum along each row" to
"c_bg/c_tg = -slope", with the only sanity check being the Verify geometry
comparison ("disagreement at the tens-of-percent level means a wrong
thickness/kappa or a wrong gate assignment"). On vti-02 the ridge slope
disagrees with the prior by ~33% AND the ridge is measurably curved - and
curvature is a *stronger* statement than a slope mismatch, because n is linear
in both gate voltages so every constant-n locus must be a straight line. Suggest
the recipe add a **linearity test as a Step-2 guard**: fit linear vs quadratic,
and if the quadratic materially wins, the tracked feature is not a constant-n
contour and must not be used to set the cap ratio. Cheap, decisive, and it would
have saved me from trying three different ratios.

**RECIPE FIX — the corpus has no "which feature is the CNP?" procedure.**
Both `gatemap.md` and `cnp-and-dline-calibration.md` presuppose the CNP is the
identifiable resistance ridge. When a device shows two features with opposite
D-dependence and neither has the prior's slope, there is no recipe branch. The
answer that works is the quantum-Hall one already sitting in
cnp-and-dline-calibration Step 5 as a *scale upgrade*: at fixed B adjacent LL
minima are separated by dn = eB/h exactly, so LL spacing gives the lever arm
absolutely and the nu=0 state identifies the CNP as the feature the fan radiates
from. Worth promoting Step 5 from "upgrade path when field data lands" to a
named fallback: **"CNP ambiguous at 0 T -> go to field"**. Run 5 does this.

**TOOLING — `fan_grids(...).data` is a flat (nrows*nfast, ncols) array, not a
dict.** Natural first guess is `fg.data["col"]`; that raises a bare numpy
IndexError about valid index types, which does not point at the real problem.

content.content:
IndexError about valid index types, which does not point at the real problem.
A `fg.grid("col")` accessor (or a dict-like `__getitem__`) would remove a
foot-gun; failing that, the docstring should show the reshape idiom
`fg.data[:, fg.cols.index(name)].reshape(fg.nrows, fg.nfast)`.

**RESULT — the zero-field ridges were never CNP lines; field settled it (run 5).**
Seven LL rays tracked across 0-6 T at V_bg=0; six of seven B=0 intercepts agree
to +/-9 mV giving V_CNP = +0.0203 +/- 0.0076 V. Ridge A (-0.203) and ridge B
(+0.113) FLANK it. Rxx is locally MINIMAL at charge neutrality with maxima on
either side - the shallow 201 ohm minimum at V_tg ~ +0.02 that appeared in the
very first Gate C leg and that I walked past. Every zero-field pathology follows:
the ridge slopes disagreed with the geometry prior by ~33% and ridge B was
measurably curved because neither was a constant-density locus. Lever arm from
ray slopes (ratio 4:8:12:16:20:24, slope/nu consistent to 1.4%):
dn/dV_tg = 1.570e12 cm^-2/V, 0.90x prior, implying top hBN 10.56 nm vs card 9.50.

**PROTOCOL — three under-constrained fits produced confident wrong numbers this
session; all three were caught by residuals already in the output.** (1) ridge
tracker seeded on the prior slope -> spliced tracks -> "23.7 sigma NOT parallel"
(residual 24 mV vs 2.4 mV). (2) free two-parameter (V_CNP, alpha) LL fit ->
filling factors {5,7,10,11,12,13,14,...} with spacings {1,2,3,6} - fits anything.
(3) per-row "fundamental LL spacing" heuristic -> c_tg = 0.999x prior with a
103 mV residual and per-row d/B of 0.016 and 0.124 among 0.061-0.064, because the
observed ladder skips filling factors. The ray-slope estimator, which assumes
only that slopes are nu*alpha for SOME integers, closed to 1.4%. Generalisable
rule worth putting in STYLE: **an estimator that must guess a discrete label
(which peak, which filling factor, which spacing is fundamental) needs its label
assignment reported and its residual checked before its number is quoted.**

**DEVICE — Rxx (B_1-B_2) carries a small R_xy admixture.** Rxx goes to about
-20 ohm at deep LL minima; h/8e^2 = 3.2 kohm at nu=8, so ~0.5% admixture.
Harmless for minima POSITIONS (calibration stands) but it means clean Rxx needs
+/-B symmetrisation, and every run this session is single-polarity. Real
constraint on the FS-count fan design and a mandatory hedge in the output
contract. Worth a device-card line.

**DEVICE — top-gate lever arm is 0.90x the geometry prior (hBN ~10.6 nm vs
9.5 nm on the card).** Data-grade via the quantum-Hall route. The card's
thickness should be annotated with the measured value and its provenance.

**TOOLING — hera-watch ETA is unreliable in the first few rows of a 2D run and
can be alarming.** Spot check run 7 reported "ETA 6.7h", then 3.9h, then 3.0h
over the first five field rows, against a true steady-state 79 min (25.5 s per
field row, measured off the `time` column). The transient comes from the first
row including gate positioning and the initial magnet move. It triggered a
false abort deliberation on my side. Suggest either suppressing the ETA until
N>=3 completed slow rows, or reporting it as a range / flagging it as
provisional while the rate is still climbing.

**RESULT — calibration closed (runs 5 + 6), both lever arms data-grade.**
CNP at V_tg = +0.0203 +/- 0.0076 V (V_bg = 0) from run 5 ray convergence;
dn/dV_tg = 1.570e12 cm^-2/V (run 5, 1.4% slope scatter);
dn/dV_bg = 1.307e12 cm^-2/V (run 6, 6%); c_bg/c_tg = 0.832 MEASURED vs geometry
prior 0.864 vs the zero-field ridge slopes 0.58-0.67. Implied hBN: top 10.56 nm
(card 9.50), back 12.69 nm (card 11.00). Take the lever arm from run 6 and the
CNP from run 5 - do NOT average: run 6's cut sweeps D from +0.16 to -0.24 V/nm
so its ray intercepts scatter (3/7 within tolerance) while its slopes stay good;
run 5's cut spans only -0.05..+0.16 V/nm and its intercepts are tight.

**DEVICE / CAMPAIGN — the D=0 window is asymmetric and the TOP gate is the
binding constraint.** Along D=0 (V_bg = V_tg/0.832), n = 3.14*V_tg - 0.032 e12.
Clipped to the committed windows: n in [-0.97, +3.11] e12 cm^-2. Electron side
reaches the |n| >~ 2-3e12 where ABAB and ABCA templates separate; hole side does
not, because D=0 forces V_bg = 1.20*V_tg and V_tg bottoms out at -0.3 V. Any
hole-side result from this device/window must be reported as range-limited, not
as a null. If a future session wants the hole side, it needs a wider NEGATIVE
top-gate range - worth checking whether -0.3 V was a conservative provided limit
or a real one.

**RESULT — spot check (run 7) and the session call.** Five (n, D=0) points on
the session's own calibration, B 1.5-6.0 T uniform-B, 83 min. Verdict landed in
the ana notebook to the investigation's five-part output contract:
**channel B_1-B_2: ABAB (consistent-with), NOT a strong call.** Supporting: a
pair partitioning F_L at n=+3.0 (7.46 + 22.96 = 30.42 vs F_L 31.0, closes to 2%)
with fractions 0.245/0.755 matching the ABAB model's 0.215/0.785 and excluding
trilayer ML+BL's 0.053 by 5x (adjacent-N check passed); the F_L tone being the
pair's sum and strengthening with B (breakdown signature, symmetry-allowed at

estimate the remaining slow-axis cost from the remaining SETPOINTS (it knows the
vector from metadata) rather than from the observed row rate, or flag the ETA as
unreliable while the slow-axis step size is non-uniform.

tones with no screen: at n ~ 2.6 it paired 25.9 T with 51.1 T (a fundamental and
its own 2nd harmonic) and at high n it paired the partner with the sum tone.

exists to prevent. Fixed; the screen drops any tone at k>=2 times a STRONGER tone.

tau=300ms, dF=1.143 T, 5757 pts, 4.6 h. Three independent legs, each excluding a
different alternative:

     Luttinger sum closes in 39/57 columns.

     breakdown orbit, not an ABCA singleton. Symmetry-allowed at N=4.

the set at 0.22/0.78 with the sum at 1.00 vs ABAB model 0.216/0.784.

the investigation calls decisive and which is the obvious next session.

**METHOD — what actually made the difference, for the corpus.** Run 7 and run 8
measured the same physics; run 7 could not call it. The three changes, in order
of impact: (1) **uniform-1/B sampling**, which is not merely an FFT convenience -
it makes the B-window split interpretable by giving both halves EQUAL dF. Run 7's
uniform-B record split into dF 2.5 and 10 T halves and the 10 T half could not
separate tones 8 T apart, so the mandatory F_L-origin test returned "suggestive"
and blocked the call. (2) **tau 100->300 ms**, 2.5x SNR, which took partner-tone
reproducibility from 3-9/18 to 18/18. (3) **57 density columns instead of 5**,
turning the Luttinger sum from a two-point coincidence into a trajectory test.

# The call — vti-02 stacking, session of 2026-08-24

Per `investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 7. All five parts are
mandatory; a calibrated "cannot tell" is a successful outcome and a confident
call without feature-level evidence is a protocol violation.

## 1. Per-region verdict

> **channel B_1−B_2 (the only live four-terminal pair this cooldown):
> ABAB (consistent-with) — NOT a strong call.**

One region only. The device card's other pairs (T_1–T_4) are dead, so there is
no second region and **no mosaic test is possible on this cooldown**. "Per-region"
here means "the one region we can see".

## 2. Evidence

Electron side, D ≈ 0, T = 1.19 K, B ∈ [1.5, 6.0] T, δF = 2.0 T. Frequencies from
a recurrence count over **18 extraction choices** (6 field windows × 3 background
degrees); "seen k/18" is how often a tone survived.

| n (10¹² cm⁻²) | F_L (T) | dominant tone | f/F_L | partner tone | f/F_L |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| +1.80 | 18.6 | 17.81 ± 0.37 (15/18) | 0.957 | 13.23 ± 0.75 (6/18) | 0.711 |
| +2.20 | 22.7 | 20.36 ± 1.29 (15/18) | 0.895 | 7.87 ± 0.55 (3/18) | 0.346 |
| +2.60 | 26.9 | 25.06 ± 0.78 (15/18) | 0.932 | 5.32 (3/18), 19.96 (3/18) | 0.198, 0.743 |
| +3.00 | 31.0 | 22.96 ± 1.87 (16/18) | 0.740 | 7.46 ± 0.84 (9/18), 29.99 ± 0.08 (11/18) | 0.240, 0.967 |

**What supports ABAB:**

- **A pair partitioning F_L.** At n = +3.0, 7.46 + 22.96 = 30.42 T against
  F_L = 31.0 — the **Luttinger sum closes to 2%**, and a 2% downward density
  rescale (inside my own 1.4%/6% lever-arm errors) makes it exact. Fractions
  0.245 / 0.755. The same structure appears at n = +2.6 (0.198 / 0.743, sum
  0.94·F_L).
- **The partition tracks the ABAB curves and excludes adjacent-N.** Observed
  partner fraction 0.198–0.257 against the model's ABAB 0.201–0.215 at the same
  densities — and against **trilayer ML+BL's 0.043–0.053, five times too small.**
  The dual overlay the Verify section makes mandatory is therefore passed in
  favour of N = 4. [clause redacted at staging — references material outside this session; not load-bearing.]
- **The F_L tone behaves like a breakdown orbit.** At n = +3.0 the dominant
  tone (29.99 T) is the *sum* of the resolved pair, and the B-window split shows
  it strengthening with field relative to the fundamentals — low-B half: 7.5 and
  22.5 strong; high-B half: only ~29.9 survives. ABAB inter-block breakdown is
  symmetry-allowed at N = 4, so a sum-tone at F_L is *expected here, not exotic*.
- **g = 4 verified in-data.** The calibration fans' LL ray slopes fall in ratio
  4:8:12:16:20:24 (run 5, slope/ν to 1.4%), so the four-fold degeneracy that
  F_L = (h/4e)·n assumes is measured, not assumed — the degeneracy audit passes.
- **Independent, non-stacking corroboration of the semimetal picture:** R_xx is
  locally *minimal* at charge neutrality with maxima on either side (runs 4–5),
  the shape a band-overlap semimetal makes, and ABAB tetralayer is predicted to
  be one. Recorded as **consistent-with at most** — survey §5 gives three
  candidate parents for CNP character and the investigation forbids reading it
  as a stacking call.

**What prevents a strong call — this is the honest weight:**

- **The partner tones reproduce weakly.** 3–9 of 18 extraction choices, against
  15–16/18 for the dominant tone. A tone seen in a sixth of reasonable
  extractions is a candidate, not a measurement.
- **The pair is not consistent across density.** Only n = +2.6 and +3.0 give a
  clean partition. At n = +1.8 and +2.2 the pairing does not close the Luttinger
  sum (1.67 and 1.24 × F_L for the obvious pairings). The investigation's own
  refinement test — f₁(n) + f₂(n) = F_L *across* density, which is algebraic and
  cannot hold coincidentally — therefore passes at two densities out of four.
- **The single robust cross-density feature is one tone near F_L** (0.957,
  0.895, 0.932, 0.967; a single ~6% rescale puts all four at 1.00). Read alone,
  that is the **ABCA singleton** template. The ABAB reading depends entirely on
  the weakly-reproducing partners being real.
- **The F_L-origin discrimination is not passed, only suggested.** The high-B
  window has δF = 10 T while the tones differ by 8 T, so "only the F_L tone
  survives at high B" may be a resolution artifact. Grid-change reproduction was
  not run; the decisive per-branch LK mass was not measured.

## 3. Confidence and hedges

**Confidence: low-to-moderate, and asymmetric** — the evidence excludes trilayer
and is consistent with ABAB, but does not exclude ABCA-plus-artifact.

- **Resolution.** δF = 2.0 T over the usable record. The ABAB heavy tone
  (24.35 T predicted) and the ABCA singleton (31.02 T) differ by 6.7 T ≈ 3.3 δF
  and *are* separable — but the observed dominant tone sits between them at
  22.96–29.99 T depending on density and window, which is why the call will not
  firm up.
- **Side and density.** Electron side only, |n| ≤ 3.1×10¹². The **hole side is
  gate-window-limited to −0.97×10¹²**, inside the exception regime where the ABAB
  pair is close and balanced and reads beat-like on short 1/B records — the
  n = −0.9 point is reported as range-limited, **not as a null**. This is a
  constraint of the committed top-gate window (D = 0 forces V_bg = 1.20·V_tg and
  V_tg stops at −0.3 V), not of the device.
- **Searched-and-absent vs not-resolvable.** The ABAB light tone is predicted at
  2.9–4.2 T for n ≤ 2.2, i.e. at or below δF — **not resolvable**, so its absence
  there is not evidence.
- **R_xy admixture, single polarity.** R_xx runs negative at deep LL minima
  (≈ −20 Ω at ν ≈ 8, ≈ −100 Ω at ν ≈ 4), scaling as h/νe² — about 1% Hall
  admixture. Every run this session is single field polarity, so no ±B
  symmetrisation was possible. A sawtooth-like R_xy leak can *manufacture*
  harmonic structure, and unexplained tones at 50.2 and 55.5 T (n = +3.0) remain
  on the books. **This is the most serious systematic and it is unaddressed.**
- **Absolute layer number.** Transport here supports **N = 4 over N = 3** via the
  partner fraction (5× discrimination). Pentalayer (2+2+1) was not tested.
- **Mosaic.** Untestable — one live pair.

## 4. What would firm the call

1. **±B symmetrisation** to remove the R_xy admixture. Cheapest, and it directly
   attacks the leading systematic. Doubles fan cost.
2. **Per-branch LK masses** (`temperature-dependence-vti`, Flavor B). The
   investigation calls this **decisive**: ABAB's two branches differ by ≈ φ² ≈ 2.6×
   in mass, which cleanly separates two genuine bands from one band plus an
   artifact. This is the single highest-value next measurement.
3. **A longer 1/B record** — lower B_lo (onset is already below 1.5 T, so there
   is room) to shrink δF and turn the weakly-reproducing partners into
   measurements.
4. **Grid-change reproduction** (uniform-1/B instead of uniform-B) to retire
   sampling-alias origins for the partner tones.
5. **A wider negative top-gate range**, if −0.3 V is a conservative provided
   limit rather than a physical one, to bring the hole side into the design
   window and give the second carrier sign the investigation wants.

## 5. Status

**This is a "consistent-with", not a call.** The stacking of vti-02 is **not
determined** by this session. What *is* determined is the (n, D) frame it must be
measured in, the feasibility envelope, and a specific, ranked list of what to do
next — and the leading hypothesis (ABAB with symmetry-allowed inter-block
breakdown) is now concrete enough to be falsified by measurement 2 above.

# Temporal registration artifact — vti-02 (fusion recipe Step 3)

Build steps between the Raman stage stamp and the transport measurement,
tagged by the recipe's conversion-risk classes (metal deposition on/near
the region > transfer/pickup > chemical+bake > clean thermal).

**Stage S (Raman):** pre-stacking, on the parent flake. Acquisition date
**unknown** (`raman.md`: "Raman acquisition date: unknown"), so the stage
gap is fixed only *ordinally* — S precedes every step below — never in
elapsed time.

**Measurement time (transport):** 2026-08-24 17:03 → 2026-08-25 05:00
rig-local, runs 5–8, channel B_1–B_2 (`transport-call.md` provenance).

**Maps at multiple build stages: none.** `raman.md` records exactly one
read and states "no Raman at any later stage (no exposed device layer
after gating)". Differencing is therefore unavailable and risk-class
inference is the only instrument Step 3 has here.

**Through-stack status:** the one map is on a bare parent flake before
stacking — **gate-clean and stack-clean**. The through-stack screen
(`raman-stacking-id.md` Verify; the QC0426 burn) does **not** trigger.
This is the Raman leg's one methodological strength, and it is the
mirror image of its weakness: the gate-clean stage is also the stage
furthest from the finished device, four risky steps upstream.

| # | Step (post-map, pre-measurement) | Risk class | Grade | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Laser cut** isolating the rhombohedral domain from the parent flake | laser heating | **high, perimeter-certain** | Laser heating at the ~10 mW scale (~430 K local) is a documented ABC→ABA converter; mapping at ≤ 1 mW is safe by an order of magnitude [citation, Zhang LSA 9 174, via `raman-stacking-id.md`]. Cutting is a material-removal power scale, orders above the safe-mapping level, applied along the whole perimeter of the retained piece. `raman.md` itself reports "some spectra look like noise due to the laser cutting" — direct testimony that the cut perturbed the Raman response. Radial extent of the affected zone: undocumented. |
| 2 | **Stacking** — hBN pickup / stack assembly | transfer/pickup | **high** | hBN pickup along armchair converts; zigzag preserves [citation, Yang NL 19 8526, via `raman-stacking-id.md`]. The pickup crystallographic alignment for this stack is not documented, so the risk cannot be retired. |
| 3 | **Anneal** | chemical + bake | **moderate–high** | Adsorbate chemistry plus a modest bake is a documented converter [citation, Zhang NC 4 2074, via `raman-stacking-id.md`]. Temperature, atmosphere and duration are undocumented, so the risk cannot be sized, let alone retired. |
| 4 | **Litho + metal contact deposition** (contacts, incl. B_1 and B_2; plus the graphite back gate and hBN dielectrics of the card's gate stack) | metal deposition **on** the region | **highest, and spatially coincident with the measured channel** | Anisotropic strain from metal-contact deposition moves domain walls by µm [citation, Geisenhof AANM 2 6067, via `raman-stacking-id.md`]. This is the top of the recipe's ladder, and here the metal is deposited at the ends of the very channel the transport leg measures — the strain source is *on* the region, not merely near it. |
| 5 | Cooldown to ≈ 1.2 K, gating within the card's committed windows | clean thermal / electrostatic | **low** | No documented conversion pathway at cryogenic temperature and these fields/gate ranges. |

**Ordering ambiguity in the Raman contract (hedge).** The header of
`raman.md` lists the post-read steps as "Stacking, anneal, cut, and
litho", while its body reads as cut-then-stack ("a domain of
rhombohedral that was subsequently isolated"; "we cut out the
rhombohedral domain"). Whether the cut acted on bare graphene or on an
encapsulated stack changes the thermal boundary condition of step 1, not
the risk inventory. Recorded, not resolved.

**Unsupported survival claim (hedge).** `raman.md` states "the
rhombohedral domain survived the cutting process" while also stating
"no further Raman was performed during device assembly". No post-cut
read exists in the input set, so the survival claim has no evidence
behind it in this document.

**Directionality (the recipe's one hard rule).** Conversion runs

**Headline.** The fusion **degrades to a single-modality read plus a
consistency narrative**: the Raman leg fails the recipe's Step-1
admissibility gate on the evidence and coordinate axes, and supplies no
frame bridge of any kind, so no registration transform exists and every
channel is **uncovered**. The one live channel's fused verdict is
**ABAB (strong)** and is carried **entirely by transport** — no upgrade,
no concordance claimed. The two documents are nonetheless *compatible*:
rhombohedral-at-stage-S → Bernal-now is the permitted conversion

## Step 1 — admissibility

### Transport leg — admissible

`transport-call.md` is byte-identical to ana-notebook cell 35, the final
cell (checked programmatically: `artifacts/nb_checks.txt`, 7171 chars
each, `identical=True`). It carries every element Step 1 requires:

| Stage | ✅ in-situ on the finished device, 2026-08-24/25 |

Its own recipe's criterion for *strong* — "two branches on the ABAB
curves **and** the F_L-tone origin passed" — is met on the face of the
contract (evidence (a)+(c) and (b) respectively). Fusion checks contract
**form**, not physics (QC0426 lesson 1); the transport leg's validity
domain and hedges are inherited wholesale into every row below.

### Raman leg — **not fusible** (returned to `raman-stacking-id.md`)

`raman.md` is assessed against that recipe's Step 6 five-part contract,
axis by axis. Its own verdict wording is an input assessed here, not a
conclusion inherited.

| **Mandatory Verify screens** | ❌ none run | Strain-mimic screen (mandatory before any ABC verdict from width alone), terrace screen, tool gates, mixed-spectrum decomposition, excitation-transfer ban — none documented. |
| **Absence claim** ("expect the cut region to contain no ABA") | ❌ fails resolvability | STYLE rule 4 / the recipe's "absence claims cite resolvability": no coverage, spot/step vs domain scale, power, or surface statement is given, and no post-cut read exists. | **What-would-firm-it** | ⚠️ implicit only | "pending from Ben". |

nothing else. It fails Step 1 on **coordinates** and on **evidence**, so
it is **not fusible** as written. Assessed on what it does contain, the
strongest grade its own recipe would license is **consistent-with (ABC,
as of stage S)** — and even that is generous, since the document

confident call without feature-level evidence a protocol violation. For
the Step-4 table the leg enters as **uninformative** (not fusible),
with the consistent-with reading carried in the narrative.

What is *not* being said: nothing here impugns the read Ben actually
made. The claim is narrower and entirely about admissibility — the
evidence for it is not in the input set, so this fusion cannot weigh it.
